mainTopic: מומי כהנים: the danger of holding back urine, definitions of the משנה's blemishes, and the meaning of מרוח אשך
overview: The משנה lists more מומין that disqualify a כהן, including a swollen belly (כריסו צבה). The גמרא uses the swollen belly to teach that holding back urine is dangerous, so one may urinate in public rather than hold it in. Stories about שמואל and מר בר רב אשי show that this danger outweighs modesty and even embarrassment. ברייתות and statements of ריש לקיש and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל add more harms: barrenness, dropsy (הדרוקן) and jaundice (ירקון). רבי יהושע בן לוי reads the same פסוק as a lesson about students and humble prayer. The גמרא then returns to the משנה to define רוח קצרית, מאושבן and בעל גבר, and measures the organ blemish by the knee. A new משנה brings four opinions on the Torah's מרוח אשך, and the גמרא shows how each תנא rejected the earlier reading because of the word's letters. The amud ends as another משנה begins, about a כהן whose ankles or knees knock together.

steps.title: The משנה lists more blemishes of a כהן
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists body conditions that are מומין disqualifying a כהן: sagging breasts, a swollen belly, a protruding navel, epilepsy, attacks of a demon's spirit, and unusually large genitals.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are also blemishes: breasts that sag like a woman's, a swollen belly, a navel that sticks out, an epileptic (even if it only happens once in a long while), one upon whom a 'short spirit' comes (a demon's spirit, as the גמרא explains), one whose testicles are unnaturally large, and one whose member is unnaturally large.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list of מומין that make a כהן unfit to serve in the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item is a physical or medical condition, not a sin. Note the phrase אפילו אחת לימים: even rare seizures count as a מום. The swollen belly (כריסו צבה) is the item the גמרא will pick up on next.

keyTerms.meaning: an epileptic, one who has seizures
a 'short spirit': a demon's spirit that comes upon him (steps 18-19, Rashi)
one with an unnaturally large member (Rashi)

phrases.english: MISHNA:
breasts that sag like those of a woman,
his belly is swollen,
his navel protrudes,
an epileptic, even if only once in a long while,
a 'short spirit' comes upon him,
one with large testicles, and one with a large member.
phrases.notes: All are disqualifying blemishes for a כהן.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: These physical conditions are מומין that disqualify a כהן from עבודה.

steps.title: One may urinate in public but not drink in public
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בריה דרבי חייא בר אבא rules that a person may urinate in public, but a scholar should not drink water in public.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא, son of רבי חייא בר אבא, said: One may urinate in front of many people, but one does not drink water in front of many people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא picks up the משנה's swollen belly and brings a related הלכה about not holding back urine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The link to the משנה is כריסו צבה, because holding back urine can cause the belly to swell. So health and safety come before modesty here, and one may urinate publicly. Drinking in public, however, involves no danger. It is simply undignified for a תלמיד חכם, so it is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: in front of many people, in public

steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying public urination is generally fine behavior. It means that if one needs to go, one must not hold it in out of embarrassment, because that is dangerous.

phrases.english: GEMARA:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba, son of Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba, said:
one may urinate in public,
but one may not drink water in public.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands on the כריסו צבה item of the משנה by adding a related practical הלכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Holding back urine is not required for modesty's sake, but drinking in public is unbefitting.

steps.title: A ברייתא teaches the same rule
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא is quoted that says exactly what רבי אבא said.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is also taught in a ברייתא: One may urinate in public, but one does not drink water in public.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports רבי אבא's statement with a ברייתא that uses the same words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ותניא נמי הכי means an older source agrees with the אמורא. This makes the rule stronger. The ברייתא will go on to give a real-life example.

keyTerms.meaning: and a ברייתא also teaches this

phrases.english: And this is also taught in a baraita:
one may urinate in public,
but one may not drink water in public.

steps.raayaObject: רבי אבא's rule about urinating and drinking in public

steps.title: A man held back and his belly swelled
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא tells of a man who needed to urinate, held it in, and ended up with a swollen belly.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there was an incident with a man who wanted to urinate but did not, and his belly became swollen.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a story that shows why the rule exists: holding back urine is physically harmful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story ties the הלכה back to the משנה. Holding back urine can cause כריסו צבה, which is one of the מומין just listed. So the danger is real and can even cause lasting harm.

keyTerms.meaning: and there was an incident with someone
and it was found / it turned out

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the rule is based on real medical danger, not just convenience. That is why modesty gives way here.

phrases.english: And there was an incident with one
who wanted to urinate and did not urinate,
and his belly was found to be swollen.

steps.raayaObject: That holding back urine is dangerous
steps.raayaSupportSource: A real incident recorded in the ברייתא

steps.title: שמואל needed to urinate at a public lecture
steps.stepSummary: On the שבתא דרגלא, the big public lecture before a festival, שמואל needed to urinate, and people spread a sheet around him for privacy.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל needed to urinate on the שבת of the festival lecture. They spread a sheet for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story. This step is setup: it describes what שמואל did, and the next step brings the reaction to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל did not hold back, which fits the rule. But because he was important, he received special privacy with a sheet. The problem with this will be raised in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: the שבת of the festival lecture, when crowds gathered
they spread a cloak/sheet for him

phrases.english: Shmuel needed to urinate on the Shabbat of the Festival lecture,
they spread a sheet for him,

steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל relieved himself in public but with special privacy arranged.

steps.title: שמואל's father tells him to correct the public impression
steps.stepSummary: שמואל's father offers him 400 זוזים to go back and undo the impression he made. People who cannot arrange a sheet might think they must hold back, and that would put them in danger.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came before his father, who said: I will give you 400 זוזים, go and undo what you did. You can arrange privacy, but should someone who cannot arrange it put himself in danger?
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל's father criticizes the example שמואל set and tells him to publicly correct it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is not what שמואל did for himself. The problem is the lesson ordinary people might learn from it: that one must find privacy before urinating. A poor person with no sheet might then hold back and endanger himself. So שמואל must teach publicly that one does not hold back, even without privacy.

keyTerms.meaning: undo / retract the incident (correct the impression)

steps.confusionAlert: The father is not saying שמואל sinned by using a sheet. He is worried about the false lesson others might learn from seeing it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches that a leader's private behavior can become public הלכה in people's eyes. Leaders must make sure that their example does not lead others into danger.

phrases.english: He came before his father,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֶתֵּן לָךְ אַרְבַּע מְאָה זוּזֵי
phrases.english: who said to him: I will give you four hundred dinars
and go retract this incident.
You, who are able (to have a sheet spread),
but one who is not able, should he endanger himself?
phrases.notes: Rhetorical question: of course he should not.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דַּאֲבוּהּ, אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֶתֵּן לָךְ אַרְבַּע מְאָה זוּזֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to and corrects the conduct described in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's public use of a privacy sheet
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Others who cannot get privacy may conclude they must hold back, which puts them in danger.

steps.title: מר בר רב אשי urinates even with his mother-in-law approaching
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי needed to urinate while on a bridge and did so. When told his mother-in-law was coming, he said he would do it even in her ear.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר רב אשי needed to urinate while on the bridge beams, and he urinated. They said to him: Your mother-in-law is coming! He said to them: Even in her ear.
steps.whatsHappening: A final story shows how far the rule goes: danger to health beats even serious embarrassment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A mother-in-law is someone before whom one would normally be very embarrassed. מר בר רב אשי's sharp reply means the danger of holding back is so serious that he would not stop even in front of her. This puts the rule from step 2 into practice in the most extreme way.

keyTerms.meaning: on the beams of a bridge
in her ear (i.e., I would not stop even right next to her)

steps.whatToRemember: Holding back urine is dangerous, as shown by the משנה's כריסו צבה. So one may relieve oneself in public rather than hold it in, even when it is embarrassing. Leaders must also make sure their example does not lead others to endanger themselves.

phrases.aramaic: מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי אִיצְטְרִיךְ אַגּוּדָּא גַּמְלָא,
phrases.english: Mar bar Rav Ashi needed (to urinate) on the beams of a bridge,
he urinated.
They said to him: Your mother-in-law is coming!
He said to them: (I would do it even) in her ear.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי אִיצְטְרִיךְ אַגּוּדָּא גַּמְלָא
steps.raayaObject: That avoiding the danger of holding back overrides even severe embarrassment
steps.raayaSupportSource: The conduct and statement of מר בר רב אשי

steps.title: Maybe a leech caused the swelling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: maybe the man's belly swelled because of a leech, not because he held back urine.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let me say the swelling came from a leech!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא from Step 4 and questions its proof. Maybe a leech, and not holding back urine, caused the swollen belly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא was brought to show that holding back urine is dangerous. If another cause, like a leech he swallowed, can explain the swelling, then the story proves nothing about urine. The גמרא is testing whether the proof really holds.

keyTerms.meaning: "Let me derive it instead from…": the גמרא suggests another explanation
A leech, a bloodsucking worm that can get into the body

phrases.english: But let me derive (the swelling)
phrases.notes: This is the usual way the גמרא suggests a different cause.

phrases.english: because of a leech!
phrases.notes: Maybe a leech in his intestines caused the swelling

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back past the stories of שמואל and מר בר רב אשי to challenge the ברייתא in Step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that the swelling came from holding back urine
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is another possible cause, a leech, so the story does not prove that holding back urine is dangerous.

steps.title: His urine was dripping
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is talking about a man whose urine afterward only dripped, which shows the damage was to his urinary tract.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where his urine dripped.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the leech challenge with one word: the man's urine came out only in drips.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A leech would not explain a urine problem. Since his urine stopped flowing normally, the harm must have come from holding it in. So the ברייתא's proof stands.

phrases.english: Where (his urine) drips.
phrases.notes: His urine afterward came out only in drips, so the urinary tract was damaged

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the leech challenge of Step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the symptoms point to a urinary cause
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The swelling could have come from a leech.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dripping urine shows that holding it in damaged the urinary tract.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא survives: holding back urine is truly dangerous, as shown by the man's dripping urine.

steps.title: Holding back urine can make a man barren
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that a man has two openings very close together. Holding back urine can break the thin wall between them and make him barren.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A man has two openings, one that lets out urine and one that lets out seed, and only a wall as thin as a garlic peel separates them. When a man needs to urinate and holds it in, if one opening breaks through into the other, he becomes barren.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא that describes a second danger of holding back urine: it can cause infertility.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two passages are separated by a wall as thin as a garlic skin. Pressure from held-in urine can tear it, and then urine reaches the seed passage. This adds a new harm, being barren, to the swelling discussed before.

keyTerms.meaning: Openings or passages in the body
Garlic peel, used as a picture of something very thin

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
There are two openings in a man,
one lets out urine
and one lets out semen,
and between this one and that one there is nothing
except something like a garlic peel.
phrases.notes: A very thin wall

phrases.english: When a man needs (to urinate and holds it in),
if they are pierced, this one into that one,
he is found to be barren.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שְׁנֵי נְקָבִים יֵשׁ בּוֹ בָּאָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another ברייתא on the danger of holding back urine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Holding back urine can tear the thin wall between the two passages and make a man barren.
steps.whyThisMatters: It explains why שמואל's father worried about people holding back (Step 6). The danger is serious enough to override modesty concerns.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: Do not be barren, like your animals
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש reads the פסוק as hinting that a man will not be barren when he relieves himself freely, as animals do.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: What does it mean when it is written, "There shall not be a barren male or female among you or among your animals"? When will there be no barren man among you? When you act like your animals.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש finds a hint in a פסוק for what the ברייתא just taught: relieving yourself when you need to keeps you from becoming barren.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the word ״וּבִבְהֶמְתֶּךָ״ as a condition, not just as a list of who is blessed. You will not be barren if you behave like an animal, which urinates as soon as it needs to without holding back.

keyTerms.meaning: "What is the meaning of what is written": opens a reading of a verse

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"There shall not be among you a barren male or barren female
or among your animals"?
phrases.notes: דברים ז:יד

phrases.english: When will there not be a barren man among you?
At a time when (you are) "like your animals."
phrases.notes: You relieve yourself when needed, without holding back

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a פסוק that hints at the ברייתא's teaching that holding back urine causes barrenness.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not holding back, like an animal, protects a man from being barren.
steps.confusionAlert: ריש לקיש is not saying people should behave like animals in general. He means only this: do not hold back when your body needs to relieve itself.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי: Students and humble prayer
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי reads the same פסוק as a blessing: you will not lack students, and your prayers will not go unanswered, if you make yourself humble like an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: "There shall not be a barren male among you" means barren of students. "Or a barren female" means your prayer will not be barren before ה׳. When? When you make yourself like an animal.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי gives a different, spiritual reading of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For him, "barren" means having no students to carry on your Torah, or having prayers that go unanswered. The condition "like your animals" now means humility: standing before ה׳ humbly, like an animal with no pride. This moves the פסוק from a lesson about the body to a lesson about the soul.

keyTerms.meaning: Barren, here meaning unanswered or without results
"The Place": a name for ה׳, the Omnipresent

steps.whatToRemember: The same פסוק is read in two ways. ריש לקיש reads it about the body: do not hold back urine. רבי יהושע בן לוי reads it about the soul: you will have students, and your prayers will be answered, when you are humble.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
"There shall not be a barren male among you": barren of students,
"or a barren female": that your prayer will not be
barren before the Omnipresent.
phrases.notes: It will be heard and answered

phrases.english: When?
At a time when you make yourself like an animal.
phrases.notes: With humility

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: לֹא יִהְיֶה בְךָ עָקָר מִן הַתַּלְמִידִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different, spiritual reading of the same פסוק that ריש לקיש explained.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Humility, making yourself like an animal before ה׳, brings students and answered prayers.

steps.title: רב פפא: Do not urinate on earthenware or a hard surface
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא teaches that a person should not urinate onto a clay vessel or onto hard ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: A person should not urinate on an earthenware vessel, and not on a hard place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues its collection of teachings about urination. רב פפא gives a practical rule about where not to urinate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rashi explains: urine in an earthenware chamber pot is later thrown into a nearby river, and urine on hard ground is not absorbed, so it is washed down a slope into the river. Soft earth soaks it in. The reason for his concern comes in the next step, from רב.

keyTerms.meaning: a hard place, ground that does not absorb

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
A person should not urinate
phrases.notes: Literally 'should not pass water.'

phrases.english: not on earthenware vessels,
and not on a hard place,
phrases.notes: Because the urine is not absorbed and flows away.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לֹא יַשְׁתִּין אָדָם מַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another teaching to the series of statements about urination.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One should not urinate into an earthenware vessel or onto hard ground, since either way the urine ends up in the river (Rashi).

steps.title: רב's reason: Babylonia's waters flow back to עין עיטם
steps.stepSummary: רב's statement is brought as the reason for רב פפא's rule: water in Babylonia flows underground back to עין עיטם in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב said: These slopes of Babylonia send water back to the spring of עין עיטם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a statement from רב to explain why רב פפא's rule makes sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water that is not soaked into the ground is washed down the slopes into the rivers (Rashi). According to רב, these flow to עין עיטם, the spring that supplied water to the בית המקדש. So urine left on hard surfaces could end up in that holy water source.

keyTerms.meaning: the spring of עיטם, which supplied water to the בית המקדש

phrases.english: As Rav said:
These slopes of Babylonia
send the water back to the Spring of Eitam.
phrases.notes: Through underground channels to the source of the Temple's water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind רב פפא's rule.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's rule against urinating on surfaces that do not absorb
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's statement that Babylonian waters flow back to עין עיטם

steps.title: אביי: A woman should not urinate facing a child
steps.stepSummary: אביי says a woman should not urinate while facing a small child directly, but turning to the side is fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: A woman should not stand directly facing a child when she urinates. If she turns sideways, we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another urination rule, this time from אביי, about a woman and a young child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is only about standing directly in front of the child. Turning to the side removes the problem, so this is a limited rule, not a total ban.

keyTerms.meaning: we have no problem with it

phrases.english: Abaye said:
A woman should not stand
phrases.notes: While urinating.

phrases.english: directly in front of a child,
but sideways, we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הָא אִיתְּתָא לָא תְּקוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further practical rule to the collection about urination.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman should not urinate directly facing a child; turning sideways is permitted.

steps.title: Holding back waste causes dropsy and jaundice
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל teaches that holding in feces causes הדרוקן (dropsy) and holding in urine causes ירקון (jaundice).
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: Holding back feces brings a person to dropsy. Holding back the stream of urine brings a person to jaundice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a health warning about holding in one's waste.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects back to the earlier warning (steps 4 and 10-11) that holding back urine causes harm. Here רבן שמעון בן גמליאל names two specific illnesses: one from holding feces and one from holding urine.

keyTerms.meaning: a 'column' of feces that is pushed back (held in)
a 'pipe-stream' of urine that is held back

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
A column of feces that is held back
brings a person to dropsy,
a stream of urine that is held back
brings a person to jaundice.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: עַמּוּד הַחוֹזֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme that holding back waste is harmful, now naming specific illnesses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Holding in feces causes הדרוקן; holding in urine causes ירקון.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: Four kinds of buildup and four illnesses
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש lists four things that build up in the body and the illness each causes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא said in the name of רב קטינא, in the name of ריש לקיש: Too much blood brings many boils. Too much semen brings much צרעת. Too much feces brings much dropsy. Too much urine brings much jaundice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a longer list from ריש לקיש, expanding רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's idea to four kinds of buildup.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last two items match רבן שמעון בן גמליאל exactly: feces leads to הדרוקן and urine leads to ירקון. ריש לקיש adds two more: built-up blood (from not doing bloodletting) leads to boils, and built-up semen leads to צרעת.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna said,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב קַטִּינָא, אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rav Ketina said, Reish Lakish said:
phrases.notes: רב קטינא is passing on what he heard from ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: Too much blood — many boils,
too much semen — much leprosy,
too much feces — much dropsy,
too much urine — much jaundice.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא, אָמַר רַב קַטִּינָא, אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: דָּם רָבֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's two-item list into four items.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Buildup of blood, semen, feces or urine causes boils, צרעת, הדרוקן and ירקון respectively.
steps.whatToRemember: This ends the side-discussion about urination: holding things in the body is seen as causing illness.

steps.title: What is a 'shortened spirit' in the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's list of blemishes and asks what 'רוח קצרית' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'A רוח קצרית comes upon him.' What is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The side-discussion is over, and the גמרא returns to the משנה's list of blemishes that disqualify a כהן. It quotes the phrase 'רוח קצרית' and asks what it means; the answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists a person with 'רוח קצרית' as unfit for the עבודה, but the term is unclear. The גמרא is asking for a definition, not attacking anything.

keyTerms.meaning: a 'shortened spirit': the next step explains it as a demon's spirit
what are they? (asking for a definition)

phrases.english: A 'shortened spirit' comes upon him.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה.

phrases.english: What is this?

steps.triggerLanguage: רוּחַ קַצְרִית בָּאָה עָלָיו. מַאי נִינְהוּ?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the urination discussion and goes back to explaining the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of 'רוח קצרית' in the משנה.

steps.title: It means a demon's spirit has come upon him
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that 'רוח קצרית' means a 'רוח בן נפלים,' a demon-spirit, has come upon him.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: A spirit of a 'בן נפלים' has come upon him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting a ברייתא that defines the term.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'בן נפלים' refers to a demon. So the משנה is speaking about someone seized by a demonic spirit, which shows up as fits of madness (Rashi: רוח שטות), and this makes him unfit to serve.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא: רוּחַ בֶּן נְפָלִים בָּאָה עָלָיו.
phrases.english: It was taught: A spirit of a 'fallen one' (a demon) has come upon him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: רוּחַ בֶּן נְפָלִים בָּאָה עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רוח קצרית is a demonic spirit (רוח בן נפלים) that has come upon the person.

steps.title: Defining מאושבן and בעל גבר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's terms מאושבן and בעל גבר, and a ברייתא says the first is about the testicles and the second about the organ.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'The מאושבן and the בעל גבר.' It was taught: A משובן is about the testicles, and a בעל גבר is about the organ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next blemish in the משנה and uses a ברייתא to explain the two terms.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both terms describe an unusual size in the male organs. The ברייתא tells us which body part each refers to: משובן is oversized testicles, and בעל גבר is an overly long organ.

keyTerms.meaning: one with an unnaturally long organ

phrases.english: The meushban and the ba'al gever.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה.

phrases.english: It was taught: A meshuban is in the testicles,
and a ba'al gever is in the organ.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמְאוּשְׁבָּן וּבַעַל גֶּבֶר. תָּנָא: מְשׁוּבָּן בַּבֵּיצִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next blemish listed in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משובן refers to the testicles; בעל גבר refers to the organ.

steps.title: Other names for these blemishes: קיין and גרבתן
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא gives other names: משובן is also called קיין, and גרבתן is also called בעל קיק. The קיין is in the testicles and the גרבתא is in the organ.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: A משובן is the same as a קיין. A גרבתן is the same as a בעל קיק. A קיין is in the testicles; a גרבתא is in the organ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא that gives alternate names for the same blemishes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא does not add a new blemish. It links the משנה's words to other names people used. It agrees with the first ברייתא: one condition is in the testicles and the other is in the organ.

keyTerms.meaning: another name for a condition of the organ

phrases.english: It was taught: A meshuban — this is the kayyan,
the gerabtan — this is the ba'al kik;
a kayyan — in the testicles,
a gerabta — in the organ.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds other names for the same blemishes defined in step 20.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's מאושבן and בעל גבר are two size-related blemishes: one in the testicles, one in the organ. Each also has other names (קיין, גרבתן / בעל קיק).

steps.title: How long must the organ be to count as a blemish?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what length of the organ makes a כהן blemished.
steps.simpleTranslation: And up to what length?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question about the blemish just discussed, an organ that is too long. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said this blemish is in the organ, but it did not give a measurement. A rule needs a clear line, so the גמרא asks where 'too long' begins.

keyTerms.meaning: And up to how much? A question asking for a measurement

phrases.english: And up to how much?
phrases.notes: This refers to the organ blemish (בעל גבר / גרבתא) from the previous steps.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the size limit of the organ blemish named in steps 20-21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The length at which the organ counts as a disqualifying blemish.

steps.title: רב יהודה shows: until the knee
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה points with his hand and says the measure is up to the knee.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה pointed and showed: until the knee.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers by pointing to show the spot. The blemish is when it reaches the knee.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of giving a number, רב יהודה uses a body landmark, the knee. This gives a measure that anyone can check easily.

keyTerms.meaning: Pointed or showed with a gesture

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda pointed and showed:
Until the knee.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The organ is a blemish when it reaches the knee.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the knee measure
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב teaches that reaching the knee disqualifies, but stopping above the knee is fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: if it reaches the knee, he is unfit. If it stops above the knee, he is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that matches what רב יהודה said. It also spells out both sides of the line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא confirms the knee as the landmark. It makes the line exact: reaching the knee is פסול, and anything shorter is כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Unfit, disqualified from the Temple service

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
Until the knee, he is unfit.
Above the knee, he is fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב יהודה's knee measure with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's measure of 'until the knee'
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב

steps.title: Another version: until the knee is fit, below the knee is unfit
steps.stepSummary: Some say the opposite edge: reaching the knee is still fit, and only going past the knee disqualifies.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: until the knee, he is fit. Below the knee, he is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the ruling. It moves the line a little lower.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions use the knee, but they disagree about the knee itself. In the first version, reaching the knee is פסול. In this version, reaching the knee is still כשר, and only passing it is פסול.
steps.confusionAlert: The two versions do not disagree about using the knee as the landmark. The only question is whether reaching exactly the knee already disqualifies.

phrases.english: Some say:
Until the knee, he is fit.
Below the knee, he is unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another version of the ברייתא's line.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reaching the knee is fit. Only past the knee is unfit.
steps.whatToRemember: The organ blemish is measured by the knee. One version says reaching the knee disqualifies, and the other says only going past it does.

steps.title: New משנה: what is מרוח אשך?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה defines the Torah's מרוח אשך and brings three other opinions about its meaning.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If he has no testicles, or only one testicle, this is the 'מרוח אשך' in the Torah. רבי ישמעאל says: anyone whose testicles were crushed. רבי עקיבא says: anyone who has wind (swelling) in his testicles. רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says: anyone whose appearance is dark.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It gives four different explanations of the Torah's blemish called מרוח אשך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion says it means missing one or both testicles. רבי ישמעאל says crushed testicles, and רבי עקיבא says swollen testicles. רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס leaves testicles completely and says it means a dark appearance.

keyTerms.meaning: A blemish named in the Torah (ויקרא כא:כ), connected to the testicles

phrases.english: Mishnah:
If he has no testicles,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא בֵּיצָה אַחַת —
phrases.english: or he has only one testicle,
this is the 'mero'ach ashekh' stated in the Torah.
Rabbi Yishmael says:
Anyone whose testicles were crushed.
Rabbi Akiva says:
Anyone who has wind in his testicles.
phrases.notes: This means the testicles are swollen.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus says:
Anyone whose appearance is dark.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה about a different blemish.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are four opinions on מרוח אשך: missing testicles, crushed testicles, swollen testicles, or a dark appearance.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל's problem with the first opinion
steps.stepSummary: If the Torah meant missing testicles, it should have said חסר אשך.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: This was hard for רבי ישמעאל: for that meaning, the Torah should have said 'חסר אשך' (lacking a testicle)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining why each תנא disagreed. It starts with what bothered רבי ישמעאל about the first opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion says the blemish is missing testicles. The Torah has a simple word for 'missing,' חסר, and it did not use it. So מרוח must mean something else.

phrases.english: Gemara:
It was difficult for Rabbi Yishmael:
For this, it should have said 'chasar ashekh'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind רבי ישמעאל's dispute in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first opinion: מרוח אשך means missing testicles
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah would have used the clearer word חסר for 'missing.'

steps.title: So רבי ישמעאל reads it as crushed testicles
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל teaches that it means testicles that were crushed.
steps.simpleTranslation: So he teaches: whose testicles were crushed.
steps.whatsHappening: Because of that problem, רבי ישמעאל reads מרוח as 'crushed.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל connects מרוח to the root מרח, 'rubbed' or 'smeared,' which leads to 'crushed.' This is why the גמרא words it שנמרחו. This reading fits the Torah's actual word better than 'missing.'
steps.confusionAlert: The משנה wrote שנימוחו and the גמרא here writes שנמרחו. Both mean 'crushed.' The גמרא's wording is just closer to the letters of מרוח.

phrases.english: He teaches: whose testicles were crushed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי ישמעאל's reading that answers his own difficulty.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's problem with רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: If the Torah meant crushed, it should have said ממרוח אשך.
steps.simpleTranslation: This was hard for רבי עקיבא: for that meaning, it should have said 'ממרוח אשך'!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא explains why רבי עקיבא did not accept רבי ישמעאל's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the Torah meant 'crushed,' the grammar would call for the passive form ממרוח. Since the Torah wrote מרוח, 'crushed' is not an exact fit.

keyTerms.meaning: Crushed testicle, the form that would clearly mean 'crushed'

phrases.english: It was difficult for Rabbi Akiva:
For this, it should have said 'mamro'ach ashekh'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי ישמעאל's reading from step 28.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word for 'crushed' would be ממרוח, not מרוח.

steps.title: So רבי עקיבא reads it as wind in the testicles
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא teaches that it means wind (swelling) in the testicles.
steps.simpleTranslation: So he teaches: that there is wind in his testicles.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא hears the word רוח (wind) inside מרוח and reads it that way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letters of מרוח contain רוח, wind. So רבי עקיבא explains it as testicles swollen as if filled with air.

phrases.english: He teaches: that the wind is in his testicles.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי עקיבא's reading that answers his difficulty.
steps.terutzMaskana: מרוח means wind (swelling) in the testicles.

steps.title: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס's problem with רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: If the Torah meant wind, it should have said רוח אשך.
steps.simpleTranslation: This was hard for רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס: for that meaning, it should have said 'רוח אשך'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס did not accept רבי עקיבא's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the Torah meant wind, it could have just written רוח without the extra מ. The extra letter shows that 'wind' is not the exact meaning either.

phrases.aramaic: קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס:
phrases.english: It was difficult for Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus:
For this, it should have said 'ruach ashekh'!

steps.triggerLanguage: קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי עקיבא's reading from step 30.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For 'wind,' the Torah would have written רוח without the מ.

steps.title: So רבי חנינא reads it as a dark appearance
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס teaches that it means one whose appearance is dark.
steps.simpleTranslation: So he teaches: whose appearance is dark.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס gives a completely different meaning: a dark appearance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reading is no longer about testicles at all. It is hard to see how this comes from the words, and the next step explains how he gets it.

phrases.english: He teaches: whose appearance is dark,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי חנינא's reading that answers his difficulty.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מרוח means wind in the testicles.
steps.terutzMaskana: מרוח אשך means a dark appearance.

steps.title: His method: take away letters, add letters, and explain
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא holds that we may move letters between words to explain a verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that we subtract letters, add letters, and explain the verse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי חנינא gets 'dark appearance' from the verse. He uses the method of גורעין ומוסיפין ודורשין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Take the ח from מרוח and give it to אשך. Take the א from אשך and give it to מרוח. The words now read מראו חשך, 'his appearance is dark.'

keyTerms.meaning: He holds, meaning this is his view
We take away letters, add letters, and explain the verse

steps.whatToRemember: Each תנא in the משנה rejected the earlier reading because the Torah's word מרוח did not fit it exactly. רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס reaches 'dark appearance' by moving letters between the two words.
steps.whyThisMatters: גורעין ומוסיפין ודורשין is a known method of reading verses. Here it explains an opinion that at first seems to have no source in the words.

phrases.english: He holds that we subtract, add, and expound.
phrases.notes: The ח of מרוח moves to אשך, and the א of אשך moves to מרוח. This gives מראו חשך, 'his appearance is dark.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how רבי חנינא's reading in step 32 comes from the verse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס holds that letters may be removed and added to explain a verse.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The 'dark appearance' reading comes from moving letters: מרוח אשך becomes מראו חשך.

steps.title: Isn't a dark-skinned person already the same as a כושי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס: his reading of מרוח אשך as dark-skinned seems identical to כושי, which the משנה lists separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is the same as a כושי (a person with very dark skin)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the explanation from Step 32. If מרוח אשך means someone whose appearance is dark, the משנה would be listing the same blemish twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A later משנה (45b) already lists a כושי, a very dark-skinned person, as a blemish. Under רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס's reading, the term מרוח אשך would just repeat that case. A list of blemishes should not count the same thing twice, so his reading looks wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: That is the same as. A formula that says two cases are really one
A person with extremely dark skin, listed in the משנה as a blemish for a כהן

steps.confusionAlert: The word הַיְינוּ is not a neutral statement. It is a challenge: 'your explanation makes this the same as another case, so it is redundant.'

phrases.english: But that is the same as a Kushi (very dark-skinned person)!
phrases.notes: Refers to the כושי listed in the משנה on 45b.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס's explanation of מרוח אשך from Step 32.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס's reading of מרוח אשך as a dark-looking person
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Redundancy. The reading turns מרוח אשך into the same blemish as כושי, which the משנה already lists separately.

steps.title: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס does not include כושי in the list
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס's version of the משנה does not list כושי, so there is no repetition.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס does not teach 'כושי' as a separate blemish in the משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. In רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס's version of the משנה, כושי is not listed separately, so מרוח אשך is the only place this blemish appears.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge only works if both terms appear in the same list. The answer removes that assumption: the כושי clause belongs to the version of the other תנאים. For רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס, the dark-skin blemish is taught only through the words מרוח אשך.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not teach (that clause). His version of the teaching does not include it

steps.whatToRemember: There were four readings of מרוח אשך: missing testicles (the first opinion in the משנה), crushed testicles (רבי ישמעאל), wind or swelling in the testicles (רבי עקיבא), and a dark appearance (רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס). The last one does not repeat כושי, because רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס does not list כושי at all.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus
does not teach 'Kushi' (as a separate blemish).
phrases.notes: In his version of the משנה, the dark-skin blemish appears only as מרוח אשך.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס לָא תָּנֵי ״כּוּשִׁי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the redundancy challenge from Step 34.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different text version: the תנא's version of the list leaves out the clause that seemed repeated.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed every תנא had both מרוח אשך and כושי in the list, which would make רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס's reading repetitive.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס does not list כושי, so for him מרוח אשך is where the dark-skin blemish is taught.

steps.title: New משנה: a כהן whose ankles or knees knock together
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה lists more blemishes, starting with a כהן whose legs bend inward so that his ankles or knees hit each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who knocks his ankles together, or his knees together (as he walks).
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins and continues the list of physical blemishes that disqualify a כהן from Temple service. The first new case is someone whose legs are so crooked that his ankles or knees strike each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a new chapter, just the next משנה in the same chapter about blemishes of a כהן. The case is someone whose legs are crooked, so the ankles or the knees bang together as he walks (Rashi describes two opposite shapes). Either form counts as a disqualifying blemish.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. Marks the start of a new משנה section

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who knocks his ankles, or his knees (into each other as he walks),
phrases.notes: Rashi: with the ankles, his knees bow outward and his ankles knock together as he walks; with the knees, the reverse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion of מרוח אשך and starts a new משנה continuing the list of blemishes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן whose ankles or knees knock together because his legs are crooked has a blemish that disqualifies him from Temple service.
